lblName: TOSS (loft) attack: run in low, pull up at the pull-up point (PUP) and release climbing, so the bomb flies on to the target while you turn away. The Mode knob to the right picks what the right half shows.
lblSelections: Selections: the target steerpoint (TGT STPT), the reference the DED uses (VIP or VRP) and the delivery. Only LAT (low-altitude toss) is planned.
lblProfName: Profile: a drawing of the attack, and the map around the target with every point of it.
lblIngressData: Ingress Data: the sliders for the run-in: speed, height, G, turn direction and the OA2 to PUP distance.
lblReleaseData: Release Data: the sliders for the toss: release angle (the climb at release), release speed and release height.
lblHeadingsData: Headings Data: the angle off and the attack heading, which set the approach heading and where the pull-up point lies.
lblExtraInfo: Extra Info: true airspeed at release, the MAP distance (target to pull-up point) and the bomb's range, worked out from your sliders.
lblDeliveryMode: LAT (low-altitude toss): release in CCRP. Designate the target, hold the pickle button and pull up; the jet releases the bomb at the right moment in the climb.
lblDeliveryMode2: MAT (medium-altitude toss) would be released in DTOS (dive toss). The Planner plans LAT only, so this line is for reference.
lblMode: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
lblProfileSelect: Turns the Mode knob straight to Profile: the drawing of the attack and the map around the target.
lblDEDDataSelec: Turns the Mode knob straight to DED Data: the figures for the jet's DED, and whether the target shows in the HUD.
lblShowSelections: Turns the Mode knob straight to Selections: the target steerpoint, the reference and the delivery.
pnlSelections_Up: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
pnlSelections_Middle: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
pnlSelections_Down: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
pnlBlocked_1: VIP is blocked: the IP STPT has no position in this mission. Pick another IP STPT, or press IP STPT at the VRP. The page plans from the VRP.
lblReference: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblRefDown: VRP: the DED lines are measured from the target (TGT-TO-VRP, TGT-TO-PUP), and the run-in starts at the VRP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblRefUp: VIP: the DED lines are measured from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another): VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP. VRP needs no IP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
pnlRefUp: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
pnlRefDown: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblIP_elv: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblTGT_elv: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblTGT_E: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position; feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known.
lblTGT_N: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position; feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known.
lblTGT_EW: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position; feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known.
lblTGT_NS: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position; feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known.
btnIpAtVrp: IP STPT at the VRP (VRP mode): puts a steerpoint on the VRP and plans this attack as VIP from it, after one question. Finish the Input Panel first: the steerpoint stays where it is placed, so a later change moves the attack but not the steerpoint. Save to DTC writes it; delete it on DTC → STPT (Change on its row, Clear, Apply). In VIP mode it moves the IP STPT it created.
numIPpoint: VIP only: the steerpoint you overfly as the visual initial point — the jet's VIP (LIST 3). The jet steers to it; VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP and the offsets are measured from it. It follows the target (TGT STPT − 1) until you pick another. Shown in VIP mode, and while VIP is blocked so an IP can be picked.
lblIPpoint: VIP only: the steerpoint you overfly as the visual initial point — the jet's VIP (LIST 3). The jet steers to it; VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP and the offsets are measured from it. It follows the target (TGT STPT − 1) until you pick another. Shown in VIP mode, and while VIP is blocked so an IP can be picked.
lblIPelv: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblTGTelv: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblIPelv2: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblTGTelv2: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblIP_EW: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only); feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known. Hidden in VRP mode; empty when there is no IP.
lblIP_NS: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only); feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known. Hidden in VRP mode; empty when there is no IP.
numWaypoint: TGT STPT: the steerpoint the attack is planned on, 1 to 25; the IP is the one before it unless you pick another in IP STPT (VIP only). A new mission or flight sets it once to your first strike steerpoint; after that it is yours.
lblTGTwp: TGT STPT: the steerpoint the attack is planned on, 1 to 25; the IP is the one before it unless you pick another in IP STPT (VIP only). A new mission or flight sets it once to your first strike steerpoint; after that it is yours.
lblIPCoordinate: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only); feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known. Hidden in VRP mode; empty when there is no IP.
lblTarget: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position; feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known.
lblIP_N: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only); feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known. Hidden in VRP mode; empty when there is no IP.
lblIP_E: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only); feet north and east (kft) while the theater is not known. Hidden in VRP mode; empty when there is no IP.
lblDelivery: Delivery knob: LAT (low-altitude toss) is the one this page plans; MAT is greyed, as it was in WDP. Clicking the knob keeps it on LAT.
lblMAT: MAT, the medium-altitude toss: not planned by this page, and it cannot be chosen.
lblLAT: LAT, low-altitude toss: run in low, pull up at the PUP and let the bomb go in the climb, well short of the target. Ingress Height 100 to 2,000 ft.
pnlDelivery_Up: Delivery knob: LAT (low-altitude toss) is the one this page plans; MAT is greyed, as it was in WDP. Clicking the knob keeps it on LAT.
pnlDelivery_Down: Delivery knob: LAT (low-altitude toss) is the one this page plans; MAT is greyed, as it was in WDP. Clicking the knob keeps it on LAT.
lblZoomText: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
trbZoom: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
lblZoom: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
btnPPTnr: Show PPT Nr / Hide PPT Nr: writes each pre-planned threat's number beside its ring on the map, or takes them off. The threats are your cartridge's.
Panel1: The map's key: the target a red square, the VIP a blue square or the VRP a blue circle, the pull-up point (PUP) a magenta ring, OA1 and OA2 green triangles; the white line is the run-in the jet flies.
btnSaveMap: Saves this map as a JPEG on the BMS PC: a Save window opens on the SavedMaps folder (WDP's own, when WDP is on the PC), named TOSS.jpg.
picSatView: The attack drawn on the theater map round the target, as every map draws it: target red square, VIP blue square or VRP blue circle, PUP magenta ring, OA1 and OA2 green triangles, the run-in line; your route with its numbers, threats in red rings; the foot names the attack and the TGT STPT.
pnlBlocked_2: VIP is blocked: the IP STPT has no position in this mission. Pick another IP STPT, or press IP STPT at the VRP. The page plans from the VRP.
pnlRef_Up: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblRefVIP: VIP: the DED lines are measured from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another): VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP. VRP needs no IP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblRefVRP: VRP: the DED lines are measured from the target (TGT-TO-VRP, TGT-TO-PUP), and the run-in starts at the VRP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblRef: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
pnlRef_Down: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
picProfile: Falcas's drawing of the toss for your reference and turn direction.
lblE: Sets the attack heading to east, 90°.
lblS: Sets the attack heading to south, 180°.
lblW: Sets the attack heading to west, 270°.
lblN360: Sets the attack heading to north, 360°.
lblN: Sets the attack heading to north, 0°.
lblAttackHdgVal: Attack Heading: your heading from the pull-up point to release, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270.
trbHeading: Attack Heading: your heading from the pull-up point to release, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270.
lblAngleOff: Angle Off: how far you turn at the VRP, from the approach heading onto the attack heading, 0 to 90°. Click 0, 30, 60 or 90 under the slider to set it.
trbAngleOff: Angle Off: how far you turn at the VRP, from the approach heading onto the attack heading, 0 to 90°. Click 0, 30, 60 or 90 under the slider to set it.
lblOa2ToPupVal: OA2 to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point OA2 lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. The VRP is laid the same distance out from OA1.
trbOa2ToPup: OA2 to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point OA2 lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. The VRP is laid the same distance out from OA1.
lblTurnVal: Turn To Target: which way you turn at the VRP onto the attack heading, left or right. It sets the side the VRP lies on, and the Approach Heading.
trbTurn: Turn To Target: which way you turn at the VRP onto the attack heading, left or right. It sets the side the VRP lies on, and the Approach Heading.
lblIngrCasVal: Ingress speed: your calibrated airspeed on the run-in and into the pull-up, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. With the G it sets the turn radius.
trbIngrSpd: Ingress speed: your calibrated airspeed on the run-in and into the pull-up, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. With the G it sets the turn radius.
lblRelAngleVal: Release Angle: your climb angle when the bomb comes off, 0 to 45°. With the release speed and height it sets the bomb's range, and so the pull-up point.
trbReleaseAngle: Release Angle: your climb angle when the bomb comes off, 0 to 45°. With the release speed and height it sets the bomb's range, and so the pull-up point.
lblReleaseHeightVal: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range, 1,000 up to 13,000 ft, follows the height the pull-up reaches, worked out when Ingress Height or Pulling G's move.
trbReleaseHeight: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range, 1,000 up to 13,000 ft, follows the height the pull-up reaches, worked out when Ingress Height or Pulling G's move.
lblGVal: Pulling G's: the G of the pull-up and the turn in, 2 to 6. It sets how high the pull-up takes you, and so the Release Height range.
trbG: Pulling G's: the G of the pull-up and the turn in, 2 to 6. It sets how high the pull-up takes you, and so the Release Height range.
lblIngrHeightVal: Ingress Height: your height above the target's ground on the run-in, 100 to 2,000 ft. The VRP, PUP and OA1 ELEVs are this plus the ground under the target.
trbIngrHeight: Ingress Height: your height above the target's ground on the run-in, 100 to 2,000 ft. The VRP, PUP and OA1 ELEVs are this plus the ground under the target.
lblRelCasVal: Release Speed: your calibrated airspeed at release, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. It sets the TAS at release, and so the bomb's range.
trbReleaseSpd: Release Speed: your calibrated airspeed at release, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. It sets the TAS at release, and so the bomb's range.
lblApproachHed: Approach Heading: the heading you fly to the VRP, before the turn onto the attack heading: the attack heading turned back by the Angle Off.
lblApproachHedVal: Approach Heading: the heading you fly to the VRP, before the turn onto the attack heading: the attack heading turned back by the Angle Off.
lblAngleOffInput: Angle Off: how far you turn at the VRP, from the approach heading onto the attack heading, 0 to 90°. Click 0, 30, 60 or 90 under the slider to set it.
lblAttackHed: Attack Heading: your heading from the pull-up point to release, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270.
lblReleaseHeight: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range, 1,000 up to 13,000 ft, follows the height the pull-up reaches, worked out when Ingress Height or Pulling G's move.
lblSpeed: Release Speed: your calibrated airspeed at release, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. It sets the TAS at release, and so the bomb's range.
lblReleaseAngle: Release Angle: your climb angle when the bomb comes off, 0 to 45°. With the release speed and height it sets the bomb's range, and so the pull-up point.
lblIngressHeight: Ingress Height: your height above the target's ground on the run-in, 100 to 2,000 ft. The VRP, PUP and OA1 ELEVs are this plus the ground under the target.
lblOA2toPUP: OA2 to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point OA2 lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. The VRP is laid the same distance out from OA1.
lblIngressSpeed: Ingress speed: your calibrated airspeed on the run-in and into the pull-up, 300 to 550 kts in steps of 10. With the G it sets the turn radius.
lblTurnToTarget: Turn To Target: which way you turn at the VRP onto the attack heading, left or right. It sets the side the VRP lies on, and the Approach Heading.
lblPullingGs: Pulling G's: the G of the pull-up and the turn in, 2 to 6. It sets how high the pull-up takes you, and so the Release Height range.
lblBombrangeNmInfo: BombRange: how far a low-drag bomb travels along the ground after release, in feet and nm, for the release angle, speed and height.
lblBombrangeNmVal: BombRange: how far a low-drag bomb travels along the ground after release, in feet and nm, for the release angle, speed and height.
btnSaveDTC: Writes the four DED lines of the reference in use (VIP or VRP, PUP, OA1, OA2) into your cartridge's nav offsets and saves the cartridge now. The other reference's lines are cleared: VIP and VRP cannot be used together. Once saved, the DataCard's Delivery section becomes this attack, so the card and the cartridge agree; a save that fails leaves the card as it was.
lblTASval: True airspeed at release, in knots, for the Release Speed at the release height.
lblTAS: True airspeed at release, in knots, for the Release Speed at the release height.
lblBombrangeVal: BombRange: how far a low-drag bomb travels along the ground after release, in feet and nm, for the release angle, speed and height.
lblMAPVal: MAP: feet from the target to the pull-up point along the ground: the bomb range plus the ground the pull-up covers, and any climb on to the release height.
lblMAP: MAP: feet from the target to the pull-up point along the ground: the bomb range plus the ground the pull-up covers, and any climb on to the release height.
lblBombRange: BombRange: how far a low-drag bomb travels along the ground after release, in feet and nm, for the release angle, speed and height.
lblPUPnmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblPUPnm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblVIPnmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblVIPnm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA2nmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA1nmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA1nm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA2nm: The same range in nautical miles.
pnlDEDvip: VIP-TO-TGT (VIP reference): true bearing and range in feet from the IP to the target. TGT-TO-VRP (VRP): from the target to the VRP, where you turn onto the run-in. The number is the steerpoint the line hangs on: the IP STPT for VIP, the TGT STPT for VRP.
lblVIPelv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlBlocked_3: VIP is blocked: the IP STPT has no position in this mission. Pick another IP STPT, or press IP STPT at the VRP. The page plans from the VRP.
lblDEDRef: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblDED_Ref_VRP: VRP: the DED lines are measured from the target (TGT-TO-VRP, TGT-TO-PUP), and the run-in starts at the VRP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblDED_Ref_VIP: VIP: the DED lines are measured from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another): VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP. VRP needs no IP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
pnlDED_Ref_Down: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
pnlDED_Ref_Up: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblDEDData: The jet's DED (data entry display) nav-offset pages as they will read after Save to DTC: true bearings, ranges in feet, ELEVs in feet above sea level (0 = ground level). Every ELEV can be typed: click or tap its figure.
lblTargetHUDval: YES (green) when at release the target is under 260 mils (about 15°) below your flight path, in the HUD; NO (red) otherwise. In a toss you climb away from it, so NO is usual.
lblTargetHUD: YES (green) when at release the target is under 260 mils (about 15°) below your flight path, in the HUD; NO (red) otherwise. In a toss you climb away from it, so NO is usual.
pnlDEDvippup: VIP-TO-PUP or TGT-TO-PUP: the pull-up point, where you pull up into the toss, by true bearing, range in feet and ELEV from the IP (VIP) or the target (VRP).
lblPUPelv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlDEDvipoa1: DEST OA1: offset aimpoint 1, a point the jet marks for you on the run-in, after the turn from the VRP. Range and true bearing from the IP STPT (VIP) or the TGT STPT (VRP): offsets always hang on a steerpoint.
lblOA1elv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlDEDvipoa2: DEST OA2: offset aimpoint 2, on the run-in the OA2 to PUP dist before the pull-up point. ELEV 0 means ground level. Range and true bearing from the IP STPT (VIP) or the TGT STPT (VRP): offsets always hang on a steerpoint.
lblOA2elv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
